display.purpose: The hero headline, two unbroken lines.

headline.purpose: One per band, in the band title ink.

title.purpose: The name of a shot on its card.

lede.purpose: The two lines under the headline.

label.purpose: Stubs, the marquee, ticket headings and the stamp; always uppercase.

billing.purpose: Credits under a film name and shot numbers; uppercase, soft ink.

script.purpose: The single word after the presenter name on the feature card.

code.purpose: Commands, in the reader system monospace.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Pinned paper: lobby cards and tickets. The only blurred box shadow.

shadows.name: pointer-shadow
shadows.purpose: The pointer resting on the feature card.

shadows.name: second-ink
shadows.purpose: Text shadow on poster lettering: the off-register second ink, never blurred.

shadows.name: tack-second-ink
shadows.purpose: The same off-register device on the thumbtack.

motion.name: out
motion.purpose: The one easing curve, for arrivals and state changes.

motion.name: register
motion.purpose: The second ink of the headline and the film name slides from 0.42em -0.12em into register.

motion.name: arrive
motion.purpose: The pointer travels from -5rem 3.5rem to rest on the feature card.

motion.name: stub-state
motion.purpose: Stub ink swap and 1px lift on hover, 1px press on active.

motion.name: halftone-lift
motion.purpose: The halftone screen fades off a still while its shot plays.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: no arrival animation, 0.01ms transitions, no autoplay

narrative.overview:
The page is the glass case on the wall outside a neighbourhood cinema. Behind the glass, flat printed colour runs edge to edge, and on it hang lobby cards: pale card stock, a thin ink border, a thumbtack, a small tilt. Every card holds a real still of a film the tool made from a live page. The reader is a passer-by deciding whether to buy a ticket, so the controls are ticket stubs and the commands sit on tickets.

It is a printed world. Colour is ink laid flat, one ink per band, with no gradients and no glass. Lettering is fat poster type with a second ink printed slightly out of register. The only soft thing on the page is the shadow a pinned card throws on the wall behind it. Density is generous: five bands, each with one job, each large enough to be read from across the street.

The system is honest by construction. A card may only frame footage that exists, and work that has not shipped is stamped as in production and shown as line drawings, never as stills.
keyCharacteristics: One flat ink owns each whole band; cards and tickets are the only pale objects on it.
Card stock is a constant: it does not change between the light and dark schemes.
Poster lettering carries a hard, unblurred second ink offset down and to the right.
Every control is a ticket stub with a perforated short edge.
Stills are real frames; a halftone screen covers the printed still and lifts while film plays.
The second ink registers once on arrival; nothing animates on scroll.

rules.name: The One Ink Per Band Rule
rules.body: A band is one flat ink from edge to edge. No gradient, no texture, no second field inside it. The only things that sit on a field are type, hairlines, cards and tickets.

rules.name: The Card Stock Rule
rules.body: Cards, tickets and stubs are printed objects lit by the case. Their stock, ink and soft ink never change with the colour scheme.

rules.name: The Red Stays Red Rule
rules.body: At night the hero is still a red field. It darkens; it does not turn grey, black or blue.

rules.name: The Large Vermilion Rule
rules.body: Vermilion against stock, in either direction, is for poster-size lettering only (3.4:1). Small red text on stock uses tack red (5.3:1).

rules.name: The Second Ink Rule
rules.body: Poster lettering is printed twice: once in its own colour and once in the band's register ink, offset 0.045em right and 0.05em down with no blur. The offset is a misregistered print, so it is always hard-edged, always the same direction, and only ever applied to Bowlby One. The thumbtack and the pointer carry the same device.

rules.name: The Script Once Rule
rules.body: Yesteryear appears once per card, for the presenter's line. It never sets a heading, a label or body text.

rules.name: The Billing Block Rule
rules.body: Archivo Narrow is always uppercase and letterspaced. It is for credits, numbers and controls, never for sentences.

rules.name: The Pinned Paper Rule
rules.body: Only paper casts a shadow. Fields, bands, the marquee, stubs and type never lift.

dos: Do give each band one flat ink and set its field, text, title and register roles together.
Do put photographs and film only inside a lobby card, on stock, with its ink border and tack.
Do use real frames from a real take, kept beside a record of their source.
Do state a shot's real number and duration on its card.
Do stamp unshipped work as in production and draw it in line, on the green field.
Do make every control a ticket stub with a visible focus outline and a 2.5rem minimum height.
Do keep the second ink hard-edged, down and to the right, and on Bowlby One only.
Do keep card stock constant at night and let the fields darken around it.
Do keep every font and asset self-hosted.
donts: Don't frame a mock-up, a render or a placeholder as a lobby card; an empty case is honest.
Don't imply a library of films: one take exists, and the page shows one.
Don't blur the second ink, or use a soft shadow on anything that is not pinned paper.
Don't put gradients, glows or glass on a field.
Don't animate on scroll; the two arrival movements are the whole budget.
Don't let the hero turn black or grey in the dark scheme.
Don't set small text in vermilion on stock; use tack red.
Don't set sentences in Archivo Narrow, or anything but the presenter's word in Yesteryear.
Don't play sound unasked or start the film when reduced motion is requested.
